title: Wates Property Services: £65M Contract Published 115 Days Late
summary: West Lancashire awarded a £65M responsive repairs contract to Wates Construction in October 2019 but didn't publish the notice until February 2020 — 115 days late. Wates received £29.4M (8.8% of all spending) with recurring identical payments of £171K and £195K.
author: West Lancashire Council Transparency

title: Essential Fleet Services: 7 Identical £86K Payments (£604K Total)
summary: Essential Fleet Services received 7 payments of exactly £86,228.70 across 7 different dates in the Street Scene department. Total: £603,601. Routine fleet hire or duplicate processing? The same company received £1.3M total from West Lancashire.
author: West Lancashire Council Transparency

title: Weed Control at 99.4%: The Contract Just Below the Threshold
summary: RM Services Ltd won the Weed Control Services contract at £137,980 — just £780 below the £138,760 competitive tender threshold. RM Services grew 3,710% from initial £680 average to £25,910 per transaction. Was this contract deliberately structured to avoid open competition?
author: West Lancashire Council Transparency

title: Tawd Valley Developments: £21M to the Council's Own Regeneration Company
summary: Tawd Valley Developments Ltd — 100% owned by West Lancashire Borough Council — received £21M for Skelmersdale regeneration. A May 2021 spending jump of 3.4x normal raises questions. The company sits behind a £150M masterplan. Are governance arrangements adequate for this scale?
author: West Lancashire Council Transparency

title: Corporate Services: Three Consecutive Years of 4x Year-End Spending
summary: West Lancashire's Corporate Services spent 3.96x (2017/18), 4.06x (2018/19), and 4.72x (2019/20) its monthly average in March — three consecutive years of extreme year-end acceleration. The 4.72x spike is the highest departmental year-end ratio in the entire dataset.
author: West Lancashire Council Transparency

title: West Lancashire's Benford's Law Warning: The Highest Deviation in Lancashire
summary: West Lancashire's spending data deviates 8.2% from Benford's Law on digit 5 — the highest of all 15 Lancashire councils and the only one at WARNING level. Combined with 2,575 round-number payments (£36.6M), this points to systematic manual intervention in payment amounts.

title: 2,575 Round-Number Payments: £36.6M in Suspiciously Neat Figures
summary: 15.2% of West Lancashire's transactions end in '00' — fifteen times the expected rate. 2,575 payments over £5,000 are exact round numbers totalling £36.6M. The highest round-number proportion of any Lancashire council.

title: Matrix SCM: £8.8M Across Two Councils and 11,000 Transactions
summary: Matrix SCM Ltd receives £4.2M from West Lancashire (5,648 transactions) and £4.6M from Preston (5,445 transactions). Combined: £8.8M across 11,000+ transactions for agency staffing without cross-council benchmarking.
